Person/Shunsuke Suzuki/GitHub/ghtkn — CLI for short-lived GitHub App user access tokens (suzuki-shunsuke/ghtkn).

CLI that mints short-lived (about eight-hour) GitHub App user access tokens through the device authorization flow, stores them in the OS secret manager, and prints or injects them for tools such as GitHub/CLI (GH_TOKEN).
Intended for interactive local development (not CI): only a GitHub App client ID is required in config—no client secret or app private key for ordinary use.
See and for how ghtkn fits mise’s GitHub token stack (including credential_command and mise’s own experimental native OAuth).

A running survey of writerDecks: single-purpose writing machines, typically a full mechanical keyboard bolted to an ePaper display and nothing else. No browser, no notifications, no second application to switch into.
Späti owns a Micro Journal Rev. 2 and keeps his own build notes at My Distraction-Free Typewriter (Micro Journal).

The tension the note keeps circling: focus and productivity are not the same purchase. A typewriter delivers the first without promising the second. Späti's suggestion is that a Neovim setup configured to behave like a typewriter gets past that limit.
Micro Journal — Un Kyu Lee. The note traces back to Cassidy Williams' Building the Micro Journal.
Framedeck — cyberdeck built around a Framework mainboard.
USB Typewriter — kits for wiring a real typewriter up as a USB keyboard.

Zerowriter Ink — hot-swappable mechanical keyboard, low profile. Un Kyu Lee recommends it over the Android-based options, whose screen timeouts and notifications break the flow the device was bought to protect.
AlphaSmart — the 1990s classroom ancestor of the whole category.
Boox Palma — phone-sized, 6 GB RAM, ships with the Play Store, so Obsidian installs directly and runs in Vim mode. Typing experience walkthrough.
Boox Note Air2 — 10.3" for something closer to a page.
